name: The Glass Horizon (worked example)
description: A populated science-fantasy example with two plotlines, scenes, characters, places, notes, and a relationship.

project.title: The Glass Horizon
project.author: Sample Author
project.description: When a cartographer discovers the horizon is a machine, she must choose between repairing her dying city and freeing the intelligence trapped inside it.

books.title: The Glass Horizon
books.subtitle: Book One
books.summary: Mara maps a forbidden region and uncovers a civic conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Broken Compass
chapters.summary: Mara's instrument points beyond the city wall.

chapters.title: Beyond the Wall
chapters.summary: The expedition crosses into unmapped light.

chapters.title: A Voice in Glass
chapters.summary: The horizon speaks through Mara's compass.

chapters.title: The Council's Map
chapters.summary: Mara finds proof the danger was engineered.

scenes.title: The needle turns
scenes.summary: Mara demonstrates a compass that points toward the forbidden horizon.
scenes.content: Open on the survey hall at dawn. The ordinary compasses agree; Mara's prototype does not.
scenes.editingNotes: Plant the hairline crack in the lens.

scenes.title: Iven burns the order
scenes.summary: Iven hides the council's command to confiscate the compass.
scenes.content: He chooses Mara over his oath, but keeps the choice secret.

scenes.title: Crossing the white line
scenes.summary: The team steps beyond the last official marker.
scenes.content: The sky refracts into geometric bands. Mara hears a pulse through the compass casing.

scenes.title: The horizon answers
scenes.summary: A trapped intelligence identifies Mara by her mother's name.
scenes.content: The revelation turns a geographic mystery into a family one.

scenes.title: The hidden commission
scenes.summary: Iven admits the council sent him to sabotage the expedition.
scenes.content: His earlier protection now reads as guilt as well as loyalty.

scenes.title: Open the horizon
scenes.summary: Mara frees the intelligence, accepting an unknown sky.
scenes.content: The city loses its shield and gains a world.

characters.name: Mara Venn
characters.summary: A precise cartographer who distrusts intuition.
characters.description: Mara measures everything because uncertainty cost her mother an expedition. Her external goal is to repair the horizon; her inner need is to accept that maps are choices, not truth.

characters.name: Iven Ro
characters.summary: A council archivist divided between loyalty and conscience.
characters.description: Iven was assigned to watch Mara but believes the council has hidden too much.

fields.name: Strength
fields.value: Remembers any map he has seen

places.name: Survey Hall
places.summary: The official center of accepted geography.
places.description: A circular brass room whose floor is the city's master map.

places.name: Western Wall
places.summary: The last place where the sky looks ordinary.
places.description: White stone markers count down to zero at the sealed gate.

places.name: Horizon Engine
places.summary: A planetary machine mistaken for the edge of the world.
places.description: Concentric planes of glass bend light around the city and imprison a navigation intelligence.

fields.name: Rule
fields.value: It can communicate only through directional instruments

notes.name: Continuity checklist
notes.summary: Recurring details to track during revision.
notes.description: The compass crack grows after each contact. Iven never lies directly; he omits. The geometric sky is visible only past marker three.

notes.name: Theme
notes.summary: A map is an argument about what matters.
notes.description: Every major choice should contrast safe certainty with meaningful uncertainty.

relationships.description: Mara trusts Iven's memory but not his council allegiance.
